the extent of lithium absorption is reduced by a high fat meal.
high fat meals decrease lithium bioavailability and this effect is not related to the presence of food in the gastrointestinal tract.

the study of the effect of high fat diet on the steady state bio availability of lithium carbonate in manic depressive patients in a self-control, cross-over, design.
the effect of high fat content in food on the bioavailability of lithium.
the effect of high fat diet on steady state bioavailability (SSBA) of lithium carbonate in manic depressive patients.

high fat food reduces the steady state bio-availability of lithium carbonate.
high fat food intake may decrease the extent of lithium bioavailability in man.

a diet high in fat content may reduce the bioavailability of lithium and this could be an important factor in lithium non-responders and in patients who have to be maintained on high doses of lithium.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the extent of lithium bioavailability is reduced in patients of manic-depression, if lithium is administered along with a high fat meal.
a high fat meal significantly decreases lithium absorption.
the extent of lithium absorption is reduced by high fat food, which is in accordance with our previous findings in normal volunteers.

lithium is not absorbed as efficiently from a high fat meal.
the effect of fat on lithium absorption is not consistent and that the magnitude of the effect may vary between individuals.
